Hey /v/FinalFantasy,

Welcome to the first edition of Music Mondays! Some of us on the mod team are musicians (I personally play violin and piano) and decided that we would like to see a weekly discussion of the music that helps make series so wonderful. Even if you're not a musician, feel free to join the discussion since I know that we can all appreciate the music in one way or another.

To me, the music in Final Fantasy is great at both setting the atmosphere and also at making the experience more emotional. Most of the pieces are also good standalone music, thus the large number of orchestras that play Final Fantasy arrangements. Plus, the music makes good study music and whenever I have exams (like last week) I always find myself listening to Nobuo Uematsu or Yoko Shimomura (not FF but still great).

For the first Music Monday, and with Voat Plays Final Fantasy starting up, I thought it would be fitting to make my pick of the week the Main Theme of the Final Fantasy series. I think that the Main Theme (aka "Opening Theme" or "Prologue") really defines the series. It is not very complex, but through its simplicity it still invokes a sense of adventure and makes me want to get into the game. In the words of Nobuo,

The theme from Final Fantasy is basically the song I'd like to be remembered by. I think it's very soft and warm, but there's a strength to it. It’s appealing and I think it's the most important song in terms of everything I’ve ever done.

The original from FF1

An arrangment from Tour de Japon featuring a special guest conductor

Now I would like to open it up for discussion. Please feel free to discuss anything from what the piece means to you and what you like/dislike about it, to music theory and how the different parts interact with one another.

NOTE: If you would like to promote a cover of your own, please message the mod team and we will try to work it into a future Music Monday.

In his first act as Prime Minister, Xavier Luc Duval has announced that a large portion of the National Mauritian Army is to stand down and become reservists. There are 26,500 troops currently raised as a result of the recent threat of nuclear war between Russia and the West. As there is currently a ceasefire and a peace deal appears to be imminent, the Mauritian government sees no reason to have a large force currently active. The National Mauritian Army will therefore be reduced to 3,000 active personnel. The increase of troops from before the Russia situation is due to the re-colonisation of the Chagos Archipelago in the near future. The coastguard will also be increased from 500 members to 1,000. This is to help police the waters around the Chagos islands and to help protect the newly formed Chagos Bank Marine Reserve. The Mauritian government has thanked the young men who volunteered for the army when war seemed imminent, and thanks them for continuing to serve their nation as either coastguard, reservists or as part of the army itself.
